one_liner: Flattens 50 dimensions into 2–3 while keeping neighbours together, then finds dense groups without being told how many.
plain_explanation: UMAP takes data with fifty columns and squeezes it down to two or three, trying to keep neighbours as neighbours. Think of flattening a crumpled sheet of paper without tearing it — points that were close stay close, and the overall shape survives. HDBSCAN then finds clusters in that flattened space by looking for dense regions. Unlike k-means, you do not tell it how many clusters to find, and it is allowed to say 'this point belongs to no cluster'. Together they answer: do our clients fall into natural groups, and do subscribers sit anywhere in particular?
reference: McInnes, Healy & Melville, UMAP (2018); Campello, Moulavi & Sander, HDBSCAN (2013); McInnes & Healy, hdbscan (2017)

workflow.label: Build the k-NN graph
workflow.detail: For each client, find its 15 nearest neighbours in the full (one-hot, scaled) feature space.

workflow.label: Convert to fuzzy memberships
workflow.detail: Turn distances into probabilities. Each point's local scale is set so it has a consistent neighbourhood size.

workflow.label: Symmetrise
workflow.detail: Reconcile 'A says B is a neighbour' with 'B says A is not'.

workflow.label: Optimise the low-dim layout
workflow.detail: Place points in 2D/3D so the low-dim graph matches the high-dim one.

workflow.label: Mutual reachability distance
workflow.detail: Inflate distances in sparse regions so noise cannot bridge clusters.

workflow.label: Build the hierarchy
workflow.detail: Minimum spanning tree → condensed cluster tree.

workflow.label: Extract stable clusters
workflow.detail: Keep clusters that persist across density thresholds.

formulas.name: Local fuzzy membership (UMAP)
formulas.caption: ρᵢ is the distance to the nearest neighbour, so every point is certainly connected to at least one other. σᵢ is solved per point so that Σⱼ p_{j|i} = log₂ k — this is what makes UMAP adapt to varying local density.

formulas.name: Symmetrisation
formulas.caption: Probabilistic OR: an edge exists if either endpoint claims it.

formulas.name: Low-dimensional similarity
formulas.caption: a and b are fitted from min_dist. Heavy tails let distant points stay distant without dominating the loss.

formulas.name: Cross-entropy objective
formulas.caption: The first term pulls neighbours together; the second pushes non-neighbours apart. Keeping both is why UMAP preserves global structure better than t-SNE.

formulas.name: Mutual reachability distance (HDBSCAN)
formulas.caption: core_k(x) is the distance from x to its k-th nearest neighbour. Points in sparse regions get pushed apart, so noise cannot act as a bridge between two real clusters.

glossary.means: distance to x's k-th nearest neighbour (k = min_samples = 10)

formulas.name: Cluster stability
formulas.caption: How long a cluster survives as the density threshold tightens. HDBSCAN keeps the set of clusters maximising total stability — this is what replaces choosing k.

assumptions.text: Meaningful distance in the feature space
assumptions.evidence: One-hot encoding makes Euclidean distance crude for categoricals (every level mismatch costs the same); Gower distance would be an alternative.

figures.caption: 8,000 clients in 3D UMAP space. Drag to orbit; hover a point for the client card.

figures.title: 2D map by subscription
figures.caption: Subscribers do not form their own region. They are concentrated in some islands more than others, but AMI between clusters and subscription is only 0.042.

figures.title: 2D map by cluster
figures.caption: 26 clusters, 0.3% of clients labelled noise. min_cluster_size=250, min_samples=10 — set before looking.

figures.title: Condensed tree (HDBSCAN hierarchy)
figures.caption: Each bar is a candidate cluster, from the density at which it splits off (top) to where it dissolves (bottom). HDBSCAN keeps the teal ones: the set with the greatest total stability (f6).

figures.title: Cluster profiles in plain language
figures.caption: Each profile lists the three features that deviate most from the overall population. Generated from the data, not written by hand.

figures.title: Clusters vs known variables
figures.caption: The clusters align most with month (AMI 0.63) and barely with subscription (0.042).
